text: Cytosolic DNA is a danger signal that triggers type I interferon responses in mammalian cells. DNA induces interferons via cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP), which binds and activates the adaptor protein STING. Using biochemical fractionation and quantitative mass spectrometry, researchers identified a cGAMP synthase (cGAS) belonging to the nucleotidyltransferase family. cGAS overexpression activated transcription factor IRF3 and induced interferon-β in a STING-dependent manner. Knockdown of cGAS inhibited IRF3 activation and interferon-β induction by DNA transfection or DNA virus infection. cGAS bound DNA in the cytoplasm and catalyzed cGAMP synthesis. These results indicate that cGAS is a cytosolic DNA sensor that induces interferons by producing the second messenger cGAMP.
